name: What bathroom remodel changes trigger hidden damage in older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: What bathroom remodel changes usually reveal hidden damage in older Los Angeles homes?
mainEntity.text: What bathroom remodel changes usually reveal hidden damage in older Los Angeles homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest hidden-damage risks appear when a bathroom remodel goes beyond surface replacement. Opening walls, removing old tile, moving plumbing, or replacing a shower pan can reveal long-standing moisture problems, rot, mold, corroded pipes, outdated electrical, or damaged framing. Older Los Angeles homes are especially prone to these issues because many have had partial repairs over time rather than full system upgrades. The more layers a bathroom has built up over the years, the more likely demolition will expose surprises. Homeowners should prepare for this by budgeting a contingency, asking the contractor how hidden conditions are handled, and making sure the scope defines what happens if damage is found. It also helps to ask whether the contractor will inspect subflooring, framing, and plumbing before final finish work begins. If the remodel includes a shower replacement, that is one of the most common moments when concealed water damage becomes visible.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hidden damage is most often uncovered when a remodel opens walls or floors, moves plumbing, or removes old waterproofing. In older Los Angeles homes, contractors may find rot, prior leaks, outdated wiring, corroded pipes, uneven framing, or damaged subfloors once demolition begins.
